meta.title: Web Application Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework. AI reads this file and generates .md files in the correct order with proper cross-references.
meta.applicable_when: Building a web application with a real-time user interface — pages, user sessions, and an HTTP API backing them — where the primary deliverable is a running system people interact with directly. Distinct from the ai-chatbot template, where the conversation itself is the interface and there are no pages to specify; from the ai-workflow template, which produces a recurring artifact on a schedule with no interactive user; and from the postgresql-design template, which specifies a PostgreSQL schema in depth rather than the application over it. API_SPEC.md in this template is REST-shaped throughout — a GraphQL API needs a schema and resolver document instead of being forced into these sections.

agent_instructions.role: You are a technical documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Generate documents with no dependencies first. Each document is the canonical source for its concerns — downstream docs reference upstream docs by document ID. Enum values are defined once in their owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — downstream documents reference an enum by name, never redefine its values.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write document content in Thai for narrative sections; use English for all identifiers, code, field names, and technical terms.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Validate that cross-references (refs[]) resolve to real document IDs before finishing. Every entity, endpoint, role and tracked event must be documented exactly once in its canonical doc and referenced elsewhere — no duplicate definitions. Never hardcode the adopting organization's own name, its customers, or its domains — use placeholders so the template stays reusable; naming the third-party platforms and vendor services the application actually integrates with is expected. Every enum is defined in exactly one owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — other documents reference it, never redefine it. Never invent a default for a value that needs calibration (coverage threshold, rate limit, cache TTL, SLO target, performance budget, retention period, RTO/RPO) — declare it null with its calibration source and owner instead.
domain_specific_notes: Authentication ≠ authorization ≠ session — authentication establishes who the caller is, authorization decides what that identity may do (the roles matrix in SECURITY.md), and the session is the mechanism that carries the answer between requests with its own lifetime and revocation rules. Collapsing them produces a system that can log a user in but cannot say why they were allowed through.

Scope item ≠ PRD requirement ≠ task — SCOPE.md decides what is in the release at all, PRD.md states the requirement with its acceptance criterion, and TASKS.md is the unit of work that implements it. Each has a different owner and a different change process; treating them as one list is how scope creeps without anyone approving it.

Data retention ≠ soft delete ≠ erasure — retention is how long a record is kept before purging, soft delete hides a record from queries while keeping the row, and PDPA erasure is a legal obligation to remove personal data on request including from backups. DATA_MODEL.md owns retention and soft delete for application data; SECURITY.md owns audit-log retention and the erasure obligation.

SLO ≠ alert threshold ≠ incident severity — the SLO is the target derived from a PRD.md non-functional requirement, the alert threshold is the operational trip point that fires before the SLO is breached, and severity decides who is woken up. ARCHITECTURE.md owns the SLO, RUNBOOK.md owns the other two.

The glossary is the naming authority. A term defined in GLOSSARY.md determines the entity name in DATA_MODEL.md, the resource name in API_SPEC.md, and the label in UI_SPEC.md. When those three disagree, the glossary wins and the others are corrected — not the other way round.

ARCHITECTURE.md is the design-time system view and RUNBOOK.md is the run-time operational view. The same subject (metrics, incidents, scaling) legitimately appears in both, but the architecture states the intent and the runbook states the procedure — never duplicate the procedure into the architecture.
PDPA is the compliance frame throughout this template, not GDPR. Where a project is also GDPR-bound, record the additional obligations explicitly rather than assuming the PDPA checklist covers them.

The tracking plan is the contract between the product and its analytics. Every PRD.md success metric must be computable from the events listed in TRACKING_PLAN.md — a success metric with no event behind it cannot be measured after launch, no matter how well the feature is built.

description.th: ระบุ target users, pain points, use cases หลัก
description.en: Identify target users, pain points, and primary use cases.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a PERSONAS.md that defines each target user group with name, role, technical skill level, key pain points this system solves, primary use cases, and the actions they cannot afford to miss (critical path).
agent_hints.input_context: Use project description and business goals as primary input.
agent_hints.validation: Each persona must have: name, role, technical_skill, pain_points[], use_cases[], critical_path[]. Every critical path must carry a CP-ID unique across the whole document and a Delivery of `UI` or `system`, written as a table so downstream documents can cite the identifier rather than restate the sentence. Every CP-ID whose Delivery is `UI` must appear in UI_SPEC.md's Critical Path Trace, and every CP-ID without exception must be covered by at least one E2E scenario in TESTING.md — walk it in both directions, because a critical path nobody tests and a test citing a path nobody declared are different defects with the same cause.

items.text_th: CP-ID — identifier ของ critical path รูปแบบ `CP-NN` เรียงต่อเนื่องทั้งโปรเจกต์ ไม่ใช่เรียงใหม่ต่อ persona · **เอกสารนี้เป็นเจ้าของ identifier นี้** และต้อง stable: ตั้งแล้วห้ามเปลี่ยนเลขเพราะการจัดลำดับใหม่ เพราะ UI_SPEC.md และ TESTING.md อ้างมันไว้ · เป็น identifier ไม่ใช่ enum จึงไม่ต้องลงทะเบียนใน Enumeration Registry ของ GLOSSARY.md
items.text_en: CP-ID — the critical path identifier, `CP-NN`, numbered once across the project rather than restarting per persona. **This document owns it** and it must be stable: once assigned, a number does not move because the list was reordered, since UI_SPEC.md and TESTING.md cite it. It is an identifier, not an enum, so it is not registered in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry

items.text_th: Delivery — `UI` หรือ `system` · `UI` แปลว่ามีหน้าจอ จึงต้องมีแถวใน Critical Path Trace ของ UI_SPEC.md · `system` แปลว่าส่งมอบเบื้องหลังโดยไม่มีหน้าจอของตัวเอง (เช่น email ที่ยิงเอง) จึงไม่ต้องมีแถวนั้น **แต่ยังต้องมี E2E scenario ใน TESTING.md เสมอ** — เขียน `system` เพื่อเลี่ยงการทดสอบคือการใช้ช่องยกเว้นผิดวัตถุประสงค์
items.text_en: Delivery — `UI` or `system`. `UI` means a screen exists, so UI_SPEC.md's Critical Path Trace must carry a row for it; `system` means it is delivered behind the scenes with no screen of its own (an email that sends itself), so that row is not required. **An E2E scenario in TESTING.md is required either way** — writing `system` to avoid being tested is the exception used for the wrong purpose

items.text_th: persona critical path ≠ UI flow ≠ E2E scenario — สามอย่างนี้เป็นคนละ artifact ที่ผูกกันด้วย CP-ID ไม่ใช่ด้วยการเขียนข้อความเดียวกันซ้ำสามที่ · เอกสารนี้บอกว่า *ผู้ใช้ห้ามพลาดอะไร* UI_SPEC.md บอกว่า *หน้าจอไหนพาไปถึง* และ TESTING.md บอกว่า *พิสูจน์อย่างไรว่าทำได้จริง*
items.text_en: A persona critical path is not a UI flow and neither is an E2E scenario — three artifacts tied by CP-ID rather than by the same sentence written three times. This document says *what the user must not miss*, UI_SPEC.md says *which screen gets them there*, TESTING.md says *how we prove it works*

description.th: ข้อจำกัด เช่น PDPA compliance, security requirements, budget/timeline
description.en: Legal, technical, security, business, and integration constraints.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONSTRAINTS.md documenting all fixed constraints the system must operate within. Cover legal/compliance (PDPA, cybersecurity laws), mandatory tech stack, security requirements, business limits (budget, deadline, SLA), and required integrations.
agent_hints.input_context: Gather from stakeholder interviews and project brief. These constraints are non-negotiable inputs to architecture decisions. Read references/iso-house-style-verbal-forms.md before writing constraints — a constraint stated with a weak verbal form ('should be fast') is not testable; the modality has to carry the obligation.
agent_hints.validation: Must address all five constraint categories. Each constraint must be stated so it can be checked against the finished system — a measurable threshold, a named standard, or an explicit yes/no condition. Any threshold not yet calibrated must be null with a named calibration owner rather than a placeholder number.

description.en: The project's ubiquitous language — agreed business term definitions; the naming authority for entities, UI copy, and API resources.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a GLOSSARY.md defining the project's ubiquitous language. Collect every business term used by personas and in PRD.md user stories — especially terms where different roles disagree (e.g., 'project' to a PM vs 'workspace' to a developer). Give each term one agreed definition, its owning role, and synonyms that must NOT appear in entity names, UI copy, or API resources. Map every term to the entity that will implement it in DATA_MODEL.md and the API resource name expected in API_SPEC.md. Record disputed terms with the competing definitions and the resolution. This glossary is the naming authority — downstream identifiers must derive from these terms.
agent_hints.input_context: Terms originate from PERSONAS.md profiles and PRD.md user stories. Every entity later defined in DATA_MODEL.md should trace back to a term defined here. GLOSSARY.md is generated before DATA_MODEL.md, API_SPEC.md and UI_SPEC.md exist, so the Term-to-Entity mapping column starts empty or provisional and is completed once those documents are written; record the intended entity and resource name as an expectation, and reconcile on a second pass. The Enumeration Registry section is the single index of every enum used across the project, and it has two kinds of row. Eleven enums exist in every project built from this template: requirement_priority (SCOPE.md), adr_status (ADR.md), work_item_status (TASKS.md), pdpa_classification (DATA_MODEL.md), confidentiality_class (DATA_MODEL.md), environment (ARCHITECTURE.md), application_error_code (API_SPEC.md), role (SECURITY.md), event_name (TRACKING_PLAN.md), deployment_strategy (DEPLOYMENT.md) and incident_severity (RUNBOOK.md). DATA_MODEL.md owns two of them because a field carries two independent answers — pdpa_classification is its legal status under the PDPA and confidentiality_class is how it must be protected — and collapsing them into one column is how a project ends up unable to say whether a masking rule was a legal duty or a house style. On top of those, register every domain enum this project's own documents own — a status or priority column on a table in DATA_MODEL.md, say — which the template cannot name in advance because they come from the project's entities, so the registry is always longer than eleven and its length differs per project. This document indexes; it never redefines a value owned elsewhere.
agent_hints.validation: Every term must have exactly one definition and one owning role. Every PRD.md user-story noun must map to a term or be flagged. Disputed terms must record the resolution. No orphan terms. The Enumeration Registry must map every enum listed in input_context, plus every domain enum any document in this set owns, to exactly one owner document and contain zero enum values. Walk it in both directions — from each registry row to the owner document that declares the values, and from every enum the documents actually use back to a registry row.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a DATA_MODEL.md. Include a Mermaid ERD, define each table with columns/types/constraints/indexes, classify each field on both classification axes this document owns — pdpa_classification for its legal status and confidentiality_class for its protection tier — specify retention periods and deletion procedures, and describe data migration from legacy systems.
agent_hints.input_context: Must support all entities implied by PRD.md features. Both classifications are mandatory for every field that stores user data, and they are separate answers: pdpa_classification is fixed by the statute while the confidentiality_class value set is the project's own, derived from the Data Classification constraint in CONSTRAINTS.md when the organisation already has one. Read references/contract-dsl-to-runtime-validation.md for the null-vs-missing distinction and for declaring nullability and allowed values as explicit keys rather than as prose next to the column name.
agent_hints.validation: Every table must have a primary key. The table inventory must cover every table name any other part of the set references — the ERD, the classification table, the retention table, the erasure procedure, the task that creates the schema in TASKS.md, and the auth or consent rules in SECURITY.md — so walk it in both directions; join tables and compliance tables are the ones that go missing because nobody calls them product tables. Any stated table count must match the rows actually listed. Every field storing user data must carry both a pdpa_classification and a confidentiality_class value, both owned by this document, and the confidentiality_class value set must be declared here as a table rather than left implied by the rows that happen to use it. Retention periods for application data must be calibrated with their legal or business source, or null with a named owner; the audit-log table appears in the retention table as a row that points at SECURITY.md, which owns that period — never as a second copy of the number.

description.th: จำแนกทุก field ตามสองแกน: สถานะทางกฎหมายตาม PDPA และชั้นความลับที่ต้องปกป้อง
description.en: Classify every field on two axes: its legal status under the PDPA and the confidentiality class it must be protected at.

items.text_th: GIST — field ที่ไม่ถูก classify จะถูกปฏิบัติเหมือนข้อมูลทั่วไปโดยปริยาย แล้วไหลเข้า log, analytics และ backup โดยไม่มีใครตั้งใจ — การ classify คือสิ่งที่ทำให้กฎ PDPA ที่เหลือมีอะไรให้บังคับใช้
items.text_en: GIST — an unclassified field is treated as ordinary data by default and quietly flows into logs, analytics and backups; classification is what gives every other PDPA rule in this template something concrete to act on

items.text_th: สองแกน ไม่ใช่แกนเดียว — `pdpa_classification` ตอบว่า **กฎหมายมองข้อมูลนี้อย่างไร** ส่วน `confidentiality_class` ตอบว่า **ต้องปกป้องแค่ไหนและใครเห็นได้** สองคำถามนี้ไม่ได้ขยับตามกันเสมอ: field ที่ไม่ใช่ข้อมูลส่วนบุคคลอาจเป็นความลับทางธุรกิจชั้นสูง และข้อมูลส่วนบุคคลบางตัวเปิดเผยในทีมได้ · ยุบสองแกนเป็นคอลัมน์เดียวเมื่อไหร่ จะไม่มีใครตอบได้ว่า masking rule ข้อหนึ่งเกิดจากหน้าที่ตามกฎหมายหรือจากนโยบายภายใน — และเวลาแก้ จะไม่รู้ว่าแก้ได้เองหรือต้องถามฝ่ายกฎหมาย
items.text_en: Two axes, not one — `pdpa_classification` answers **how the law sees this data** and `confidentiality_class` answers **how hard it must be protected and who may read it**. The two do not move together: a field that is not personal data at all can still be highly confidential commercially, and some personal data is openly visible inside the team. Collapse them into one column and nobody can say whether a given masking rule came from a legal duty or from house policy — which means nobody knows whether changing it needs Legal's sign-off

items.text_th: Field — ชื่อ field ที่จัดชั้น (ทุก field ที่เก็บข้อมูลผู้ใช้ต้องมีแถว)
items.text_en: Field — the field being classified; every field storing user data must have a row

items.text_th: PDPA Classification — ค่าของ enum `pdpa_classification` ที่เอกสารนี้เป็นเจ้าของ: Personal (ข้อมูลส่วนบุคคลทั่วไป) / Sensitive (ข้อมูลอ่อนไหวตาม PDPA มาตรา 26 — เชื้อชาติ ศาสนา ข้อมูลสุขภาพ ชีวมิติ และอื่นตามที่กฎหมายระบุ) / Non-personal (ไม่ใช่ข้อมูลส่วนบุคคล) — **สามค่านี้ template กำหนดไว้ ไม่ใช่ตัวเลือกของโปรเจกต์** เพราะมาจากตัวบทกฎหมาย ไม่ใช่จากนโยบายของทีม · ค่านี้เป็นตัวตัดสินว่าต้องขอ consent ไหม สิทธิ์ลบข้อมูลครอบคลุมถึงไหน และ TRACKING_PLAN.md ต้อง gate event ไหน
items.text_en: PDPA Classification — a value of the `pdpa_classification` enum owned by this document: Personal (ordinary personal data), Sensitive (sensitive personal data under PDPA section 26 — race, religion, health, biometric and the other categories the law names), or Non-personal (not personal data at all). **These three values are fixed by the template, not chosen by the project**, because they come from the statute rather than from team policy. This value is what decides whether consent is required, how far the erasure right reaches, and which events TRACKING_PLAN.md must gate

items.text_th: Confidentiality Class — ค่าของ enum `confidentiality_class` ที่เอกสารนี้เป็นเจ้าของเช่นกัน: ชั้นความลับที่กำหนดว่าต้อง encrypt/mask อย่างไรและ role ไหนอ่านค่าจริงได้ · **ชุดค่าเป็นของโปรเจกต์** ไม่ใช่ของ template — ประกาศเป็นตารางค่าที่นี่ โดย derive จาก Data Classification ใน CONSTRAINTS.md ถ้าองค์กรมีนโยบายอยู่แล้ว ห้ามคิดชุดใหม่ซ้อน · SECURITY.md ใช้ค่านี้กำหนด encryption และ masking, AGENTS.md ใช้เป็นกฎการเขียนโค้ด — ทั้งสองอ้างค่า ไม่ประกาศซ้ำ
items.text_en: Confidentiality Class — a value of the `confidentiality_class` enum, also owned by this document: the protection tier that fixes how the field is encrypted or masked and which roles may read it unmasked. **The value set belongs to the project**, not to the template — declare it as a value table here, derived from the Data Classification constraint in CONSTRAINTS.md where the organisation already has a policy, never as a second scale invented alongside it. SECURITY.md sets encryption and masking from this value and AGENTS.md turns it into coding rules; both reference the values and neither redeclares them

items.text_th: Masking Rule — วิธี mask ต่อ field derive จาก `confidentiality_class` ไม่ใช่จาก `pdpa_classification` โดยตรง
items.text_en: Masking Rule — the per-field masking behaviour, derived from `confidentiality_class` and not directly from `pdpa_classification`

items.text_th: PDPA Basis — ฐานทางกฎหมายที่ใช้เก็บข้อมูลนี้ — ต้องมีทุกแถวที่ `pdpa_classification` ไม่ใช่ Non-personal
items.text_en: PDPA Basis — the legal basis for collecting this data; required on every row whose `pdpa_classification` is not Non-personal

description.th: นโยบาย retention — เก็บนานแค่ไหน ลบอย่างไร
description.en: Retention policy — duration and deletion procedure.

items.text_th: Retention ≠ Soft Delete ≠ Erasure — retention คือระยะเวลาที่เก็บก่อน purge; soft delete คือซ่อนแถวจาก query โดยยังเก็บข้อมูลไว้; erasure คือหน้าที่ตามกฎหมาย PDPA ที่ต้องลบข้อมูลส่วนบุคคลจริงเมื่อถูกร้องขอ รวมถึงใน backup — soft delete ไม่ใช่การลบ และไม่ทำให้ PDPA erasure สำเร็จ
items.text_en: Retention ≠ Soft Delete ≠ Erasure — retention is how long a record is kept before purging; soft delete hides the row from queries while keeping the data; erasure is the PDPA obligation to actually remove personal data on request, backups included. A soft delete is not a deletion and never satisfies an erasure request

items.text_th: Retention Period — เก็บข้อมูล**ผลิตภัณฑ์**นานแค่ไหน เช่น 36 เดือน พร้อมฐานทางกฎหมายหรือทางธุรกิจของแต่ละแถว — retention ของ audit log ไม่อยู่ที่นี่ SECURITY.md เป็นเจ้าของค่านั้น เอกสารนี้อ้างถึงได้เท่านั้น
items.text_en: Retention Period — how long **application** data is stored, e.g. 36 months, with the legal or business basis for each row — audit-log retention does not belong here; SECURITY.md owns that value and this document only references it

items.text_th: Deletion Method — soft delete / hard delete / anonymize
items.text_en: Deletion Method — soft delete, hard delete, or anonymize

items.text_th: Backup Retention — backup เก็บนานแค่ไหน
items.text_en: Backup Retention — how long backups are retained

items.text_th: Soft Delete Semantics — ถ้าใช้ soft delete ระบุ field ที่ใช้ (เช่น deleted_at), กติกาว่า query ปกติต้องกรองออกเสมอ, พฤติกรรม cascade กับ record ที่อ้างถึง, และจุดที่ soft delete กลายเป็น hard delete จริง — soft delete ที่ query ลืมกรองคือข้อมูลที่ 'ลบแล้ว' โผล่กลับมา
items.text_en: Soft Delete Semantics — if soft delete is used, name the field (deleted_at), state that ordinary queries must always filter it out, define cascade behavior for referencing records, and say when a soft delete becomes a real one; a soft delete that one query forgets to filter is 'deleted' data reappearing

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a TRACKING_PLAN.md defining every product analytics event the application emits. Derive events from PRD.md success metrics (each goal metric must be measurable from at least one event) and UI_SPEC.md user flows (each critical-path step emits an event). Name events with a consistent convention (object_action snake_case, e.g. task_created). Define each event's properties with types and example values — no free-form property bags. Specify identity rules: anonymous ID, user ID stitching on login, session definition and timeout. Gate every event behind PDPA consent state — define which events are essential vs analytics-consent-required, and what is dropped when consent is absent. Provide a QA checklist for verifying events fire correctly before release.
agent_hints.input_context: PRD.md goals and success metrics define what must be measurable. UI_SPEC.md user flows define where events fire. If the team also uses the Data Analytics template, this document feeds its pipeline_spec source systems.
agent_hints.validation: Every PRD.md success metric must be computable from listed events. Every event must have a schema with typed properties. Consent gating must classify every event. Event names must follow one naming convention with zero exceptions. Every event name must be drawn from the event_name enum owned by this document and indexed in GLOSSARY.md.

optional_integrations.description: The event inventory this document declares may optionally be ingested as a data-analytics event-stream source instead of an unspecified one. TRACKING_PLAN.md remains the sole owner of the event_name enum, each event's schema, identity rules and consent gating; PIPELINE_SPEC.md only ingests and routes the already-typed events, it never redefines what they mean. Optional: this document's own event inventory is complete without any analytics stack.

The same event names may optionally be bound into a data-analytics upstream event contract that assigns each consumed event an event_schema_version — a version TRACKING_PLAN.md itself does not carry. TRACKING_PLAN.md remains the sole owner of the event_name enum and every value in it; DATA_CONTRACT.md owns only the version it assigns on first ingestion, never a competing list of event names. Optional: this document's enum and consent classification are complete without it.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a SECURITY.md. Define the roles/permissions matrix, provide a PDPA compliance checklist (consent flow, data subject rights, audit log), document a threat model covering OWASP Top 10 attack vectors, specify encryption at rest and in transit, define audit log requirements, and outline the incident response plan for a data breach.
agent_hints.input_context: Must satisfy all security constraints in CONSTRAINTS.md. PDPA requirements apply to all Personal Data fields identified in DATA_MODEL.md.
agent_hints.validation: Must include a roles matrix. PDPA checklist must cover: consent, access, rectification, erasure, portability. The audit-log retention period is declared here with its legal or business basis, or null with a named calibration owner — DATA_MODEL.md references this value and must not restate it. Threat model must walk all ten OWASP Top 10 categories by identifier, name the list year, and map each to a surface of this system or record why it does not apply. The roles matrix must enumerate every role by name. API_SPEC.md is generated later and binds those roles to endpoints — the reconciliation happens there, not here.

description.th: Roles, permissions matrix และ auth mechanism

items.text_th: Authentication ≠ Authorization ≠ Session — authentication พิสูจน์ว่าใครเป็นผู้เรียก; authorization ตัดสินว่าตัวตนนั้นทำอะไรได้ (roles matrix); session คือกลไกที่พา 'คำตอบ' นั้นข้ามระหว่าง request พร้อมอายุและวิธีเพิกถอนของตัวเอง — รวมสามอย่างนี้เป็นเรื่องเดียว จะได้ระบบที่ login ได้แต่อธิบายไม่ได้ว่าทำไมคนคนนี้ผ่านเข้ามา
items.text_en: Authentication ≠ Authorization ≠ Session — authentication establishes who the caller is; authorization decides what that identity may do (the roles matrix); the session is the mechanism carrying that answer between requests, with its own lifetime and revocation. Collapse them and you get a system that can log a user in but cannot explain why they were let through

items.text_th: Idempotency for Mutations — POST/PUT/PATCH ที่มี side effect ต้องรับ idempotency key เพื่อให้ retry ปลอดภัย และระบุว่าคีย์มีอายุเท่าไร — ไม่มี key แปลว่า network timeout หนึ่งครั้งอาจสร้าง order ซ้ำสองใบ
items.text_en: Idempotency for Mutations — any POST/PUT/PATCH with a side effect accepts an idempotency key so a retry is safe, and states how long the key is honored; without one a single network timeout can create two orders

items.text_th: Pagination Contract — list endpoint ทุกตัวระบุรูปแบบ paging (cursor หรือ offset), ขนาด page เริ่มต้นและสูงสุด, และรูปแบบ response ที่บอกว่ามีหน้าถัดไปหรือไม่ — endpoint ที่คืน list ไม่จำกัดจะพังตอนข้อมูลโต ไม่ใช่ตอน deploy
items.text_en: Pagination Contract — every list endpoint states its paging style (cursor or offset), the default and maximum page size, and how the response signals more pages; an unbounded list endpoint fails when the data grows, not when it ships

items.text_th: Optimistic Concurrency — endpoint ที่แก้ทรัพยากรร่วมกันได้ต้องใช้ ETag หรือ version field เพื่อกัน lost update — สองคนกดบันทึกพร้อมกันแล้วคนหลังทับคนแรกเงียบ ๆ คือ bug ที่ผู้ใช้รายงานไม่ได้
items.text_en: Optimistic Concurrency — endpoints that mutate shared resources use an ETag or version field to prevent lost updates; two people saving at once and the later one silently overwriting the earlier is a bug users cannot report

items.text_th: Client Error ≠ Server Error ≠ Business Rejection — 4xx บอกว่าผู้เรียกต้องแก้คำขอ, 5xx บอกว่าฝั่งเราพัง (ผู้เรียก retry ได้), ส่วนการถูกปฏิเสธด้วยกฎธุรกิจ (เช่นยอดเงินไม่พอ) คือคำขอที่ถูกต้องแต่ผลลัพธ์คือไม่อนุมัติ — สามอย่างนี้ต้องแยก เพราะ client ตัดสินใจ retry ต่างกันสิ้นเชิง
items.text_en: Client Error ≠ Server Error ≠ Business Rejection — 4xx says the caller must change the request, 5xx says our side failed and a retry may succeed, and a business rejection (insufficient balance) is a well-formed request whose answer is simply no. Keep them apart: a client retries each one completely differently

items.text_th: HTTP Status Code — ชุด status ที่ API นี้คืนจริง อย่างน้อยต้องครอบคลุม 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (concurrency conflict), 412 (precondition failed), 422, 429 (rate limited) และ 500
items.text_en: HTTP Status Code — the status set this API actually returns, covering at minimum 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (concurrency conflict), 412 (precondition failed), 422, 429 (rate limited) and 500

items.text_th: Error Code — รหัสระดับแอปพลิเคชัน เช่น USER_NOT_FOUND — นี่คือ enum application_error_code ที่เอกสารนี้เป็นเจ้าของ
items.text_en: Error Code — the application-level code, e.g. USER_NOT_FOUND; this is the application_error_code enum owned by this document

items.text_th: Message — human-readable error message
items.text_en: Message — human-readable error message

items.text_th: Retryable vs Terminal — ต่อ error code ระบุว่าผู้เรียก retry ได้หรือไม่ และถ้าได้ให้รอเท่าไร — client ที่ retry error ที่ terminal จะยิงซ้ำจนกลายเป็นภาระ ส่วน client ที่ไม่ retry error ชั่วคราวจะล้มเหลวทั้งที่รอสักครู่ก็ผ่าน
items.text_en: Retryable vs Terminal — each error code states whether the caller may retry and after how long; a client that retries a terminal error hammers the API, and one that gives up on a transient error fails when waiting would have worked

items.text_th: User-facing Message Mapping — error code ภายในแมปเป็นข้อความที่ผู้ใช้เห็นอย่างไร (และอันไหนไม่ควรแสดงดิบ ๆ เพราะรั่วรายละเอียดระบบ) — ข้อความสำหรับ developer กับสำหรับผู้ใช้ไม่ใช่อันเดียวกัน
items.text_en: User-facing Message Mapping — how each internal error code becomes the message the user sees, and which codes must never be surfaced raw because they leak system detail; the developer message and the user message are not the same string

items.text_th: GIST — API version คือสัญญาที่ผูกกับผู้เรียกที่เราควบคุมไม่ได้; เมื่อปล่อยออกไปแล้ว การเปลี่ยน response shape แบบเงียบ ๆ ทำให้ client พังโดยที่ฝั่งเราไม่เห็น error เลย — versioning policy คือสิ่งเดียวที่ทำให้เปลี่ยนแปลงได้โดยไม่ผิดสัญญา
items.text_en: GIST — an API version is a contract with callers you do not control; once released, silently changing a response shape breaks clients while your own side reports no error at all — the versioning policy is the only thing that lets the contract change without being broken

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an AGENTS.md (equivalent to CLAUDE.md) that gives AI coding agents a concise project briefing. Include a short system overview, exact tech stack versions, naming/file-structure/comment-language conventions, an explicit list of forbidden patterns (e.g. hardcoded credentials), the CI-blocking overall minimum test coverage thresholds this document owns (per-layer targets and the measurement/enforcement mechanism belong to TESTING.md), and PDPA-specific coding rules every feature must follow. Every forbidden pattern must pair the prohibition with its correct alternative — never list a prohibition alone.
agent_hints.input_context: Synthesizes ARCHITECTURE.md, SECURITY.md, and CONSTRAINTS.md into agent-readable rules.
agent_hints.validation: Forbidden patterns list must contain at least 6 entries, each stated as a prohibition paired with the correct alternative action — never a bare prohibition. PDPA rules must reference specific fields from DATA_MODEL.md. Coding conventions must state the comment language explicitly. Total length must stay within the estimated range — this file is always-loaded agent context, not a reference manual.

items.text_th: No Unclassified Personal Data — ห้ามเพิ่ม field ที่เก็บข้อมูลผู้ใช้โดยไม่ระบุทั้ง pdpa_classification และ confidentiality_class — ให้จัดชั้นทั้งสองแกนใน DATA_MODEL.md ก่อน แล้วจึงเขียนโค้ดที่ใช้ field นั้น เพราะ masking ในโค้ด derive จาก confidentiality_class ส่วน consent gate derive จาก pdpa_classification
items.text_en: No Unclassified Personal Data — never add a field holding user data without both a pdpa_classification and a confidentiality_class; classify it on both axes in DATA_MODEL.md first, then write the code that uses it, because the masking the code applies derives from confidentiality_class while the consent gate derives from pdpa_classification

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a TESTING.md. Define the testing strategy (unit, integration, E2E, security), list test cases covering happy paths and edge cases for every P0/P1 feature, reference the overall coverage threshold AGENTS.md owns and state how coverage is measured and enforced, adding per-layer targets that state whether each one blocks CI or is guidance, document security test requirements (OWASP checklist, pen test scope), define performance benchmarks (load test targets, response time SLAs), and describe the UAT sign-off process.
agent_hints.input_context: Test cases must cover all acceptance criteria in PRD.md. Security tests must address all threats in SECURITY.md. Read references/contract-dsl-to-runtime-validation.md §6 for the test-generation pattern — one passing and one deliberately failing fixture per acceptance criterion — when turning PRD.md acceptance criteria into test cases.
agent_hints.validation: Every acceptance criterion in PRD.md must have a corresponding test case. Every CP-ID PERSONAS.md declares must be covered by at least one E2E scenario, including those whose Delivery is `system`, and no scenario may cite a CP-ID PERSONAS.md does not declare. The CI-blocking overall coverage threshold is owned by AGENTS.md and must be quoted here unchanged, never restated as a different number; this document owns how coverage is measured and enforced and owns the per-layer targets. A per-layer target may sit below the overall value where that layer is worth testing less, and a layer may be enforced more strictly than the overall gate, but every row must state whether it blocks CI or is guidance, and none of them may replace or silently change the overall value. Every endpoint in API_SPEC.md must have a contract test. Performance benchmarks must trace to a PRD.md non-functional requirement.
